title: The active no-touch register still describes promoted Network lifecycle controls as outside the WebView
observed_behavior: The current Network page exposes coordinator and worker start/stop controls, and lifecycle.commands.js deliberately performs backend dry-run, frontend confirmation, strict confirm_start/confirm_stop submission, and backend-owned command dispatch. Current-state documentation, route inventories, tests, and completed change packet MP-CHANGE-2026-0613-018 all describe this promotion. The active NO_TOUCH_BOUNDARY_REGISTER.md and browser smoke runbook still say these controls remain outside or read-only until promotion, and the register still directs operators to a manual workflow.
expected_invariant: Canonical high-risk boundary guidance must accurately distinguish frontend intent controls from backend mutation ownership after an explicitly approved promotion, so agents and operators apply the current gate instead of an obsolete prohibition or manual fallback.
root_cause: The Network lifecycle implementation and authoritative route/current-state inventories were promoted, but two canonical safety/runbook statements retained their pre-promotion text and no freshness check joins those statements to the active route/control contract.
failure_scenario: An agent follows the required no-touch register, concludes that the current guarded controls are an unauthorized boundary violation, and removes or bypasses them, or an operator follows the obsolete manual-workflow direction instead of the tested dry-run/confirmation path. Reviews can also certify contradictory ownership rules depending on which active document they read.
evidence: page-network.html lines 59-68 expose typed coordinator/worker start and stop controls
lifecycle.commands.js lines 157-200 requires a backend dry-run, matching readiness evidence, operator confirmation, and literal boolean confirm_start/confirm_stop before dispatch
CURRENT_PROJECT_STATE.md lines 44-47 says Network lifecycle is exposed only through backend dry-run and strictly confirmed routes while WebView sends intent and fingerprints
NO_TOUCH_BOUNDARY_REGISTER.md lines 181-189 and BROWSER_SMOKE_TEST_RUNBOOK.md line 230 retain the pre-promotion outside/read-only wording
CHANGE_INDEX.md identifies completed MP-CHANGE-2026-0613-018 as Promote explicit network lifecycle and current ownership/route inventories list all eight dry-run/confirmed routes
the prior comprehensive-production audit recorded this exact contradiction as invariant INV-05 but left it not_started
affected_flows: AI high-risk navigation and change review
existing_safeguards: Current project state accurately describes backend ownership
route and command ownership inventories identify the promoted controls
frontend requires dry-run and explicit confirmation
backend route contracts and provider preconditions fail closed
safeguard_gap: AGENTS.md requires agents to read the no-touch register before this high-risk work, so accurate lower-level inventories do not prevent the required canonical entry point from supplying stale direction; no doc check compares the register/runbook claim to current lifecycle routes and controls.
tests_present: tests/webview/test_webview_network_read_only_boundary.py verifies only backend lifecycle routes are used
tests_missing: active-document consistency test joining Network lifecycle no-touch/runbook wording to the current route and WebView control inventory
recommended_remediation: Update the no-touch register and browser smoke runbook to state the current boundary: WebView may stage intent and invoke the promoted dry-run/strictly confirmed routes, while the backend exclusively owns lifecycle policy, preconditions, provider calls, journal evidence, and state mutation. Retain the process-safety warning and validation gate, and add a bounded consistency check against the route/control inventory.
remediation_risk: Low for documentation changes, but wording must not imply that the frontend may decide lifecycle safety, call providers directly, or expose still-unpromoted reclaim/release/abort operations.
validation_rung: Active-document/link checks plus targeted Network mutation-boundary, route-contract, and browser smoke tests; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: The 2026-07-19 comprehensive-production audit explicitly listed this contradiction as invariant INV-05 with status not_started. W07 independently reconciled it against current exact source, current docs, inventories, tests, and the completed promotion change packet.

title: The shared API client encourages blind retry after ambiguous strict mutations and carries no stable command identity
observed_behavior: Every non-GET request is sent with only content-type and authorization headers; no caller-stable command ID is created, retained, or reused. Network loss, timeout, successful HTTP with invalid JSON, and backend COMMAND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN responses are represented as ordinary errors with generic try-again guidance, no ambiguousOutcome marker, and no commandId. A second operator action therefore creates an indistinguishable new mutation attempt.
expected_invariant: Release-critical strict mutations must preserve one request-stable identity across simultaneous submission and any ambiguous delivery outcome, label the outcome unknown, suppress blind retry advice, and reconcile or replay the same identity before permitting a new intent.
root_cause: The shared frontend request layer treats all POSTs as stateless HTTP calls and routes durable-command uncertainty through generic transport/HTTP error formatting; it has no strict-route classification, command identity lifecycle, or ambiguous-outcome state machine.
failure_scenario: A rename, publish, pipeline, audit, backend, rerun, or Network lifecycle mutation succeeds but the response is lost, times out, is invalid JSON, or returns COMMAND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. The UI tells the operator to try again and sends no stable identity, so the backend receives another independently dispatchable mutation; simultaneous clicks likewise have no shared identity or in-flight coalescing.
evidence: apiHeaders lines 243-246 adds only optional supplied headers and bearer authorization
apiRequest lines 506-526 builds every POST without a command identity and discards all request state after completion or failure
invalidJsonError/httpError and requestFailure lines 375-422 and 473-503 classify ambiguous outcomes as generic retryable errors

tests.webview.test_webview_api_client_command_replay_smoke failed every stable-identity, ambiguousOutcome, retained-commandId, unknown-outcome wording, and safe-retry assertion across simultaneous, lost-response, timeout, invalid-JSON, COMMAND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and strict-rejection fixtures
AUDIT-FIND-W01-001 independently confirms the backend also generates a fresh UUID per attempt and has no generic replay reservation
affected_flows: all strict durable WebView command routes
pipeline, audit, rerun, backend, and Network lifecycle commands
safeguard_gap: Confirmation establishes intent but not delivery identity. Generic transport formatting cannot distinguish a request rejected before dispatch from a response lost after mutation, and backend domain guards cannot replay the original terminal response or uniformly prevent a second command.
tests_present: tests/webview/test_webview_api_client_smoke.py passes invalid-JSON fail-closed checks for ordinary reads
tests/webview/test_webview_api_client_command_replay_smoke.py is a focused production-backed Node harness and currently fails with the complete ambiguity/identity matrix
tests/webview/test_webview_frontend_mutation_boundary.py verifies route ownership and confirmation payloads but not replay semantics
tests_missing: passing shared API-client tests for stable identity creation, simultaneous coalescing, ambiguous-outcome retention, definitive-result release, and same-identity retry
end-to-end frontend/backend lost-response and timeout tests proving one mutation and replayed terminal evidence across restart
recommended_remediation: Implement the frontend half of the request-stable command protocol together with AUDIT-FIND-W01-001: classify strict durable routes from authoritative contract metadata, generate one cryptographically strong command ID for a new intent, attach it in the agreed header/body field, coalesce simultaneous submissions, retain it after ambiguous outcomes, present outcome-unknown reconciliation guidance without blind retry, reuse it for explicit recovery, and release it only after a definitive terminal response. Coordinate exact fingerprint/conflict semantics with the backend reservation and replay implementation.
remediation_risk: High: a frontend-only ID without atomic backend reservation is insufficient; retaining identities after definitive rejection can block new intent, while releasing them too early or misclassifying validation failures can duplicate mutations. Secrets and stored responses must remain redacted.
validation_rung: Focused API-client replay smoke; backend handler/journal concurrency, lost-response, timeout, invalid-JSON, restart, and conflict tests; representative strict-route browser/API tests using synthetic fixtures. No source-media mutation or real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding located the shared frontend half of the replay failure. W01 established the backend root cause; W07 independently reproduced the current apiClient.js omission and unsafe retry messaging at its exact current hash.
